display_name: Wind Gap Woodruff Vineyard Pinot Noir, Santa Cruz Mountains
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Woodruff Vineyard clings to Santa Cruz Mountains ridgelines at elevations piercing the marine fog layer, where fractured shale and sandstone force Pinot Noir vines into flavor concentration. Wind Gap's 2013 and 2014 vintages earned silver medals at TEXSOM, highlighting this site's restraint over power. These wines deliver mountain minerality without coastal plumpness.",
  "wine_summary": "Wind Gap pursues balance in every release, as owner Sarah Schneider notes from her WSET training, setting them apart in California's Pinot Noir landscape. The Santa Cruz Mountains AVA spans 480,000 acres across San Mateo, Santa Clara, and Santa Cruz counties, with 85% of grapes required from this elevated terrain per 27 CFR 9.31. Woodruff Vineyard's steep slopes above the fog line shape wines with bright acidity and soil-driven focus, distinguishing them from warmer Central Coast Pinots.",
  "terroir_expression": "Shallow rocky soils of shale and sandstone, remnants of ancient seabed upheavals, drain fast on Woodruff's steep pitches, stressing vines to yield concentrated berries with mineral snap and red fruit purity. Pacific gaps funnel cool fog and winds, delaying ripeness for elevated acidity that cuts through the palate. Iron-rich red earth adds ferrous edge, translating to stony persistence in the glass.",
  "vinification_summary": "Wind Gap ferments with native yeasts and ages in neutral oak to preserve site transparency, avoiding new wood's flavor mask. Whole-cluster inclusion, a technique boosting stem-derived spice and structure, amplifies the wine's linear tension. Neutral barrels let terroir dominate, yielding balanced reds under 14% alcohol.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken—vinegar brine and cayenne meet the wine's bright shale acidity and stemmy grip for relief. Coq au vin—mushroom earthiness echoes sandstone minerality while tannins grip the braise. Grilled sardines with lemon—ocean salinity syncs with Pacific fog influence and ferrous notes. Duck confit over lentils—fat richness yields to persistent minerality and red fruit core.",
  "comparable_wines": "Mt. Eden Vineyards Pinot Noir Santa Cruz Mountains — shares high-elevation shale restraint and fog-cooled finesse. Rhys Vineyards Alpine Vineyard Pinot Noir — matches ridgeline minerality from similar fractured soils.",
  "style_profile": "Pinot Noir medium body linear structure mountain mineral backbone",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2013 now through 2028; 2014 holds to 2029. Store at 55°F away from light and vibration.",
  "value_assessment": "$40-60 retail. Competes with Mt. Eden at $55 and Rhys at $65. Worth seeking for terroir depth that outpunches generic Sonoma Pinots at this price.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers list this on California-native menus for insiders chasing mountain sites. Natural wine bars stock it for balance seekers avoiding oaky bombs. Collectors hold small allocations from Wind Gap's limited production.",
  "insider_take": "Skip if you crave plush Russian River fruit—Woodruff demands patience for its taut shale profile to unwind. Bargain hunters overlook it against flashier neighbors, missing the real Santa Cruz Mountains benchmark. Buy multiples of the 2013 for its resolved silver-medal poise.",
  "aging_potential_years": 15,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 10,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 15,

}
